comprehend.desc: post-install code signature verification and ad-hoc re-sign of each installed tool's Mach-O binaries, reported per tool in the run summary

steps.aim: add the signature-repair ladder: requirement, problem, capability, subsystem, component, file bead bound in place to lib/codesign.sh (v0.15 add-impl binds the bead itself; no separate -impl node)
wire signature repair into install: install-experience and run-report-surface gain it; bin/macacfs runs each tool through install-then-verify; lib/report.sh shows per-tool notes on ok rows
stop brenner installer side-installing pinned ntm/cass/cm into ~/.local/bin (skip flags in manifest), under a new no-side-installs requirement
LaunchAgent gets a real PATH (EnvironmentVariables) and the tick reloads its own job from a detached helper so it stays loaded
document signature repair, brenner skip flags and LaunchAgent PATH in README

edge_reasons.argv-and-usage -validated-by-> req-minim: Argument parsing admits only the closed verb+flag set and rejects anything else, so no ACFS-style provisioning or phase-runner command can ever be invoked.
edge_reasons.argv-code -validated-by-> req-minimal-sc: The argv parser code hard-codes the small verb set and errors on unknown input, enforcing in code that macacfs exposes only install, update, self-update, and schedule.
edge_reasons.bootstrap-and-self-update -validated-by-: The curl install.sh one-liner and self-update both fetch from the public GitHub repo, so that published repo with its README is the distribution surface this behavior depends on.
Running 'macacfs self-update' re-fetches the public repo and replaces the installed CLI, which is exactly the observable self-update behavior the requirement specifies.
edge_reasons.catalog-loader-code -validated-by-> req-: Loading every manifest row and offering select-all iteration is what lets 'macacfs install' reach all 39 suite tools rather than a hard-coded subset.
edge_reasons.cli-arg-dispatch -validated-by-> req-min: Restricting argv to install, update, self-update, and schedule plus global flags is the code-level enforcement of the deliberately minimal feature set.
edge_reasons.darwin-truth-per-tool -validated-by-> re: Recording verified per-tool macOS behavior, including SRPS, GIIL, and ASB lacking Darwin branches, is needed so all 39 tools actually install on a Mac.
edge_reasons.dry-run-without-sideeffects -validated-b: This problem states the dry-run must be threaded through every dispatch branch with no network installs or disk changes, which is the requirement's acceptance condition.
edge_reasons.fail-loud-aggregation -validated-by-> re: Isolating each of the 39 steps, capturing exit code and stderr, and ending with a non-zero summary exit directly embodies the no-silent-failure requirement.
edge_reasons.fb-bin-macacfs -accomplished-by-> fb-bin: The bin/macacfs entrypoint bead is realized by its concrete implementation, which wires install/update/self-update/schedule dispatch and pins the Homebrew bash shebang.
edge_reasons.fb-bin-macacfs -validated-by-> req-macos: The entrypoint enforces the macOS-only check before dispatching, so the requirement's refusal on non-darwin hosts is implemented in bin/macacfs.
edge_reasons.fb-bin-macacfs -validated-by-> req-manua: bin/macacfs dispatches the 'update' verb with optional tool selectors, giving users the manual all-tools or named-tools update the requirement demands.
edge_reasons.fb-bin-macacfs -validated-by-> req-minim: The entrypoint dispatches only install, update, self-update, and schedule, so its closed verb set is where minimal scope is concretely held in the shipped file.
edge_reasons.fb-bin-macacfs-impl -serves-> fb-bin-mac: This implementation fulfills the bin/macacfs bead, running tools then shell setup under install and guarding empty selector arrays against set -u aborts.
edge_reasons.fb-install-sh -accomplished-by-> fb-inst: The install.sh bootstrap bead is delivered by the actual install.sh file that performs the darwin check, clones the repo, and puts macacfs on PATH.
edge_reasons.fb-install-sh -validated-by-> req-macos-: install.sh performs a darwin check before cloning or installing anything, so the one-liner bootstrap itself refuses to run off macOS.
edge_reasons.fb-install-sh -validated-by-> req-public: install.sh is the curl-able one-liner served from the public GitHub repo, making it the entry point of the public distribution the requirement describes.
edge_reasons.fb-install-sh -validated-by-> req-self-u: Self-update reuses install.sh's clone-and-install path, so this bootstrap script is the mechanism that reinstalls macacfs from the freshly fetched repo.
edge_reasons.fb-install-sh-impl -serves-> fb-install-: The concrete install.sh file is the implementation artifact that satisfies the install.sh bootstrap bead.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-catalog -accomplished-by-> fb-lib: The catalog bead is realized by lib/catalog.sh, the shell code that parses share/manifest.tsv and resolves all or named tool selections.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-catalog -validated-by-> req-insta: lib/catalog.sh resolves an 'all' selection to every manifest row, which is how a bare 'macacfs install' covers the whole 39-tool suite.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-catalog-impl -serves-> fb-lib-cat: The lib/catalog.sh source file is the implementation that fulfills the catalog-loader bead's responsibilities.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-methods -accomplished-by-> fb-lib: The methods bead is delivered by lib/methods.sh, which contains the do_installer_sh, do_brew, do_cargo_git, do_go, do_npm, do_bash functions and dispatcher.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-methods -validated-by-> req-dry-r: Every install method in lib/methods.sh is dry-run-aware, so tool installs print intended actions instead of executing them when --dry-run is set.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-methods -validated-by-> req-never: lib/methods.sh only builds, installs, or upgrades binaries and never starts a service, which is where the no-daemon rule is enforced for the 39 tools.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-methods -validated-by-> req-per-t: lib/methods.sh supplies one function per install method plus a dispatcher keyed on the manifest's method field, exactly the per-tool dispatch required.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-methods-impl -serves-> fb-lib-met: The lib/methods.sh file is the concrete implementation that fulfills the install-methods bead.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-prereq -accomplished-by-> fb-lib-: The prerequisite bead is realized by lib/prereq.sh, the script that ensures Homebrew and then the rust, go, uv, and node toolchains.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-prereq -validated-by-> req-prereq: lib/prereq.sh installs missing Homebrew, rust, go, uv, and node and reports what it installed, meeting the install-not-just-report gate requirement.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-prereq-impl -serves-> fb-lib-prer: The lib/prereq.sh source file is the implementation satisfying the toolchain-prerequisite bead.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-report -accomplished-by-> fb-lib-: The reporter bead is delivered by lib/report.sh, which implements run_isolated, result accumulation, the summary table, and aggregate exit code.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-report -validated-by-> req-dry-ru: lib/report.sh renders the same table under --dry-run listing only intended actions, providing the 'prints what it would do' half of the requirement.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-report -validated-by-> req-fail-l: lib/report.sh captures each tool's rc and stderr, renders failures as ❌ rows, and returns a non-zero aggregate exit, so failures are never swallowed.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-report-impl -serves-> fb-lib-repo: The lib/report.sh file is the concrete implementation that fulfills the isolated-runner and summary reporter bead.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-schedule -accomplished-by-> fb-li: The scheduling bead is realized by lib/schedule.sh, holding state I/O, cadence calculation, plist writing, and the LaunchAgent tick entrypoint.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-schedule -validated-by-> req-fail: lib/schedule.sh tracks consecutive failures and computes weekly, nightly, or 2pm cadence from them, implementing the retry-then-escalate schedule.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-schedule -validated-by-> req-sche: lib/schedule.sh reads and writes the state file holding last-run time and status, which is the recorded run history the requirement asks for.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-schedule -validated-by-> req-week: lib/schedule.sh writes the LaunchAgent plist and reloads it via launchctl with a weekly default cadence, installing the required weekly updater.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-schedule-impl -serves-> fb-lib-sc: The lib/schedule.sh source file is the implementation that fulfills the scheduler bead.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-selfupdate -accomplished-by-> fb-: The self-update bead is delivered by lib/selfupdate.sh, which fetches the public repo into cache and atomically swaps the installed files.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-selfupdate -validated-by-> req-se: lib/selfupdate.sh re-downloads the repo and atomically replaces the installed CLI, libs, and manifest, which is the self-update behavior required.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-selfupdate-impl -serves-> fb-lib-: The lib/selfupdate.sh file is the concrete implementation that fulfills the self-update bead.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-shell -accomplished-by-> fb-lib-s: The shell-provisioning bead is realized by lib/shell.sh, containing shell_brew_bundle, shell_omz, shell_p10k, shell_tmux and the other per-action functions plus shell_run.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-shell -validated-by-> req-dry-run: Each lib/shell.sh provisioning function is dry-run-aware, so terminal setup under 'install --dry-run' changes nothing and only reports intended actions.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-shell -validated-by-> req-never-s: lib/shell.sh functions never start a daemon such as atuin's, keeping terminal-environment setup within the install-binaries-only rule.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-shell -validated-by-> req-termina: lib/shell.sh performs each ACFS-parity provisioning step, from Oh My Zsh and p10k to the brew bundle, font, zshrc, atuin, zoxide, lazygit, and ast-grep.
edge_reasons.fb-lib-shell-impl -serves-> fb-lib-shell: This lib/shell.sh implementation fulfills the shell bead, adding shell_tmux which installs ~/.tmux.conf from share/tmux.conf with a backup.
edge_reasons.fb-manifest-tsv -accomplished-by-> fb-ma: The manifest bead is delivered by the actual share/manifest.tsv data file with its 39 tab-separated tool rows.
edge_reasons.fb-manifest-tsv -validated-by-> req-inst: share/manifest.tsv lists all 39 suite tools with repo and CLI name, so it defines the complete set 'macacfs install' must put on PATH.
edge_reasons.fb-manifest-tsv -validated-by-> req-per-: Each manifest.tsv row carries a method column, which is the per-tool data the dispatcher uses to choose installer.sh, brew, cargo, go, npm, or bash.
edge_reasons.fb-manifest-tsv -validated-by-> req-pref: manifest.tsv marks MS and SRPS with the brew method, encoding the Homebrew preference for tools that publish a tap.
edge_reasons.fb-manifest-tsv-impl -serves-> fb-manife: The share/manifest.tsv file is the implementation artifact that satisfies the 39-row catalog bead.
edge_reasons.fb-plist-template -accomplished-by-> fb-: The plist-template bead is realized by share/macacfs.plist.template, the file with placeholders for program path and StartCalendarInterval.
edge_reasons.fb-plist-template -validated-by-> req-we: The plist template is the LaunchAgent skeleton that gets filled with the weekly StartCalendarInterval and installed into ~/Library/LaunchAgents.
edge_reasons.fb-plist-template-impl -serves-> fb-plis: The share/macacfs.plist.template file is the concrete asset fulfilling the LaunchAgent template bead.
edge_reasons.fb-readme -accomplished-by-> fb-readme-i: The README bead is delivered by the actual README.md describing macacfs as a mini-ACFS for Mac with install, update, and self-update usage.
edge_reasons.fb-readme -validated-by-> req-public-git: The README frames macacfs plainly as a mini-ACFS-for-Mac with only its few functions, which the public-repo requirement explicitly calls for.
edge_reasons.fb-readme-impl -serves-> fb-readme: The README.md file is the implementation artifact that satisfies the documentation bead.
edge_reasons.fb-share-atuin-guard -accomplished-by->: The atuin-guard bead is realized by share/atuin-guard.sh, the wrapper script that detects agent context and no-ops atuin history and hook calls.
edge_reasons.fb-share-atuin-guard -validated-by-> req: The requirement specifies atuin with an agent-safe shim, and atuin-guard.sh is that shim, preventing agent sessions from polluting history or hitting EPIPE.
edge_reasons.fb-share-atuin-guard-impl -serves-> fb-s: The share/atuin-guard.sh file is the concrete implementation of the agent-safe atuin wrapper bead.
edge_reasons.fb-share-powerlevel-preset -accomplished: The p10k preset bead is delivered by share/p10k.zsh, the pre-baked Powerlevel10k config copied to ~/.p10k.zsh.
edge_reasons.fb-share-powerlevel-preset -validated-by: Shipping a pre-baked p10k.zsh lets Powerlevel10k come up configured without the wizard, completing the themed-zsh part of terminal parity.
edge_reasons.fb-share-powerlevel-preset-impl -serves-: The share/p10k.zsh file is the implementation asset that fulfills the Powerlevel10k preset bead.
edge_reasons.fb-share-shell-bundle -accomplished-by->: The shell-bundle bead is realized by share/shell-bundle.tsv, listing brew formulae like ripgrep, fd, bat, eza and the Meslo Nerd Font cask.
edge_reasons.fb-share-shell-bundle -validated-by-> re: shell-bundle.tsv declares the modern-CLI Homebrew bundle and Nerd Font cask that the parity requirement lists among required terminal components.
edge_reasons.fb-share-shell-bundle-impl -serves-> fb-: The share/shell-bundle.tsv file is the concrete data artifact fulfilling the modern-CLI bundle bead.
edge_reasons.fb-share-tmux-conf -accomplished-by-> fb: The tmux-config bead is delivered by share/tmux.conf, the ACFS configuration with Ctrl-a prefix, mouse, 50k scrollback, and agent-friendly settings.
edge_reasons.fb-share-tmux-conf -validated-by-> req-t: share/tmux.conf is the ACFS tmux config installed to ~/.tmux.conf with backup, satisfying the requirement's tmux-config component.
edge_reasons.fb-share-tmux-conf-impl -serves-> fb-sha: The share/tmux.conf file is the implementation asset that fulfills the ACFS tmux configuration bead.
edge_reasons.fb-share-zshrc-mac -accomplished-by-> fb: The managed-zshrc bead is realized by share/zshrc.mac.zsh, which sources oh-my-zsh with p10k, plugins, brew shellenv, aliases, and zoxide/atuin init.
edge_reasons.fb-share-zshrc-mac -validated-by-> req-t: zshrc.mac.zsh is the mac-adapted managed zshrc installed with the prior ~/.zshrc backed up, a named component of the parity requirement.
edge_reasons.fb-share-zshrc-mac-impl -serves-> fb-sha: The share/zshrc.mac.zsh file is the concrete asset fulfilling the mac-adapted managed zshrc bead.
edge_reasons.heterogeneous-install-methods -validated: Because the 39 tools split across install.sh, Homebrew, go, cargo, npm, and bash, a naive loop fails on about nine, which motivates per-tool method dispatch.
edge_reasons.homebrew-and-toolchains -validated-by->: These helpers install Homebrew and then rustup, go, uv, and node via brew when absent, delivering the gate that installs missing toolchains rather than reporting.
edge_reasons.install-experience -validated-by-> req-i: 'macacfs install' installs all 39 tools or a named subset using each one's correct method, the observable outcome the whole-suite requirement checks.
edge_reasons.install-experience -validated-by-> req-m: The install experience is designed around Homebrew and macOS-specific per-tool methods, with no apt, systemctl, or VPS provisioning steps involved.
edge_reasons.install-experience -validated-by-> req-n: The install experience explicitly never starts any tool's server or daemon, which is what the never-start-servers requirement verifies.
edge_reasons.install-experience -validated-by-> req-p: During install the user sees Homebrew chosen wherever a tool has a tap, which is the observable form of the prefer-Homebrew requirement.
'macacfs install' first verifies and auto-installs missing toolchains before tool installs, matching the requirement that the gate installs prerequisites.
edge_reasons.install-method-functions -validated-by->: Providing do_installer_sh, do_brew, do_cargo_git, do_go, do_npm, and do_bash covers each of the roughly five methods the dispatch requirement enumerates.
edge_reasons.isolated-runner-reporter -validated-by->: Running each step in isolation without aborting, then printing a ✅/❌ summary and returning non-zero on any failure, is the fail-loud spine.
edge_reasons.launchd-scheduler-state -validated-by->: Persisting consecutive failures and rewriting the plist's StartCalendarInterval to weekly, nightly, or 2pm-daily on each fire implements the escalation policy.
edge_reasons.macacfs-command-surface -validated-by->: The command surface intentionally omits user-provisioning, OS-upgrade, service-start, and phase-runner commands, so the limited verb set is how scope is contained.
Terminal-environment setup is exposed through 'macacfs install' and refreshed by a full 'macacfs update', making the command surface the user's path to parity.
edge_reasons.manifest-store -validated-by-> req-insta: A repo-shipped TSV manifest with one row per tool plus a select-all loader gives install a complete enumeration of the 39 tools.
edge_reasons.method-dispatch -validated-by-> req-per-: Taking one catalog row and running its install or update through the matching method is the per-tool dispatch behavior the requirement defines.
edge_reasons.method-fns-code -validated-by-> req-per-: This code unit holds the per-method functions and the dispatcher that selects one by the row's method field, realizing per-tool dispatch.
edge_reasons.never-start-services -validated-by-> req: Because mcp_agent_mail, rust_proxy, and SRPS have daemon modes their installers may launch, this problem requires installing binaries only, as the requirement states.
edge_reasons.prereq-autoinstaller -validated-by-> req: Installing Homebrew first, then rust, go, uv, and node, and reporting what was installed before source builds run satisfies the auto-install gate.
edge_reasons.repo-fetch-replace -validated-by-> req-s: Cloning or pulling the public repo and atomically replacing the installed script, libs, and manifest is the core mechanism of self-update.
edge_reasons.reporter-code -validated-by-> req-fail-l: This code unit captures rc and stderr per tool, renders the ✅/❌ table, and computes the aggregate exit, so a forced failure yields non-zero.
edge_reasons.result-capture-and-summary -validated-by: Logging each step's rc and stderr to a temp file and computing an aggregate exit ensures failed tools surface with error output instead of vanishing.
edge_reasons.run-report-surface -validated-by-> req-d: Under --dry-run the end-of-run table shows only each tool's intended action and nothing is installed, the user-visible proof of side-effect-free dry-run.
edge_reasons.run-report-surface -validated-by-> req-f: Every run ends with a per-tool ✅/❌ table including captured errors and a non-zero exit on any failure, which is what fail-loud acceptance checks.
edge_reasons.schedule-state-and-plist -validated-by->: Its state file with last-run time, status, and consecutive_failures plus read/write helpers is the persisted record the run-tracking requirement needs.
edge_reasons.scheduled-update-behavior -validated-by-: The user observes weekly runs that drop to nightly after a failure and to 2pm-daily after three, returning to weekly on success, matching the requirement.
The scheduled behavior includes recording the last run's time and success or failure in a readable form, directly fulfilling run tracking.
The installed LaunchAgent runs updates weekly by default, which is the baseline cadence the weekly-LaunchAgent requirement specifies.
edge_reasons.scheduler-code -validated-by-> req-sched: The scheduler code unit's state read/write functions persist last-run and outcome after each tick, making the run history readable as required.
edge_reasons.scope-containment -validated-by-> req-mi: This problem names scope creep toward full ACFS as the main risk and demands every node trace to the four allowed features, mirroring the minimal-scope requirement.
edge_reasons.self-update-bootstrap -validated-by-> re: This problem states macacfs must self-update via the ACFS bootstrap pattern using a canonical repo URL and atomic replace, which the requirement formalizes.
edge_reasons.self-update-capability -validated-by-> r: Fetching the public repo and atomically replacing the installed CLI, via the same path as install.sh, is the capability that delivers self-update.
edge_reasons.selfupdate-code -validated-by-> req-self: This code unit performs the repo fetch and atomic replacement of the installed CLI and manifest, so 'macacfs self-update' yields the latest version.
edge_reasons.shell-assets-code -validated-by-> req-te: The shipped share/ assets, namely brew bundle, zshrc, p10k preset, tmux config, and atuin shim, are the config files parity setup installs.
edge_reasons.shell-environment-catalog -validated-by-: This declarative catalog enumerates the brew formulae, font cask, zsh components, and standalone tools that together constitute the ACFS-parity terminal.
edge_reasons.shell-fns-code -validated-by-> req-termi: lib/shell.sh's per-action functions and shell_run dispatcher are the concrete code that provisions each parity component and reports per item.
edge_reasons.shell-setup-dispatch -validated-by-> req: Routing each catalog entry to brew, cask, the omz installer, git clones, zshrc writing, or tool installs is how every parity component gets provisioned on macOS.
edge_reasons.shell-setup-experience -validated-by-> r: Terminal setup relies on Homebrew, brew casks, and a mac-adapted zshrc, keeping it on macOS-native mechanisms with no Ubuntu or systemd machinery.
Shell setup never runs 'atuin daemon' and reloads tmux only if a server is already running, so it starts no long-running service.
Under 'macacfs install' the user gets Oh My Zsh, p10k, plugins, managed zshrc, tmux config, Nerd Font, brew bundle, and atuin/zoxide/lazygit/ast-grep, i.e. parity.
edge_reasons.shell-setup-functions -validated-by-> re: These functions each perform one parity step, like cask font install, p10k clone, or zshrc write with backup, honoring dry-run and returning status.
edge_reasons.shell-spec-store -validated-by-> req-ter: The share/ data files declare the brew bundle and ship the zshrc, p10k preset, and atuin shim that the parity requirement lists as deliverables.
edge_reasons.stateful-schedule-escalation -validated-: Since launchd is stateless but the weekly-nightly-2pm cadence is stateful, this problem forces a persisted state file that rewrites the schedule, as the requirement needs.
edge_reasons.terminal-environment-parity -validated-b: This problem identifies that ACFS provisions a whole themed zsh and modern-CLI environment that macOS must reproduce, which the parity requirement then specifies.
edge_reasons.tool-catalog -validated-by-> req-install: As the single source of truth with one row per tool for all 39, the catalog defines exactly which CLIs install must place on PATH.
edge_reasons.toolchain-helpers-code -validated-by-> r: This code unit ensures Homebrew and then installs whichever of rust, go, uv, and node are missing, implementing the installing prerequisite gate.
edge_reasons.toolchain-prereqs-and-order -validated-b: Source-built tools need cargo, go, uv, or node first, so on a fresh Mac Homebrew and toolchains must be installed in order, motivating an installing gate.
edge_reasons.update-equals-reinstall-idempotency -val: Manual update re-runs each tool's latest-installing method, so idempotent in-place upgrades are what make 'macacfs update' for all or named tools safe.
